1.w: The words of King Lemuel, an oracle that his mother taught him:

2.w: O my son, O son of my womb, O son of my vows,

3.w: do not give your strength to women, nor your ways to that which ruins kings.

4.w: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine or for rulers to crave strong drink,

5.w: lest they drink and forget what is decreed and remove from all the poor their legal rights.

6.w: Give strong drink to the one who is perishing and wine to those who are bitterly distressed;

7.w: let them drink and forget their poverty, and remember their misery no more.

8.w: Open your mouth on behalf of those unable to speak, for the legal rights of all the dying.

9.w: Open your mouth, judge in righteousness, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.

10.w: Who can find a wife of noble character? For her value is far more than rubies.

11.w: Her husband’s heart has trusted her, and he does not lack the dividends.

12.w: She has rewarded him with good and not harm all the days of her life.

13.w: She sought out wool and flax, then worked happily with her hands.

14.w: She was like the merchant ships; she would bring in her food from afar.

15.w: Then she rose while it was still night, and provided food for her household and a portion to her female servants.

16.w: She considered a field and bought it; from her own income she planted a vineyard.

17.w: She clothed herself in might, and she strengthened her arms.

18.w: She perceived that her merchandise was good. Her lamp would not go out in the night.

19.w: She extended her hands to the spool, and her hands grasped the spindle.

20.w: She opened her hand to the poor, and extended her hands to the needy.

21.w: She would not fear for her household in winter, because all her household were clothed with scarlet,

22.w: because she had made coverings for herself; and because her clothing was fine linen and purple.

23.w: Her husband is well known in the city gate when he sits with the elders of the land.

24.w: She made linen garments then sold them and traded belts to the merchants;

25.w: her clothing was strong and splendid; and she laughed at the time to come.

26.w: She has opened her mouth with wisdom, with loving instruction on her tongue.

27.w: Watching over the ways of her household, she would not eat the bread of idleness.

28.w: Her children have risen and called her blessed; her husband also has praised her:

29.w: “Many daughters have done valiantly, but you have surpassed them all!”

30.w: Charm is deceitful and beauty is fleeting. A woman who fears the Lord —she makes herself praiseworthy.

31.w: Give her credit for what she has accomplished, and let her works praise her in the city gates.
